17309124.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309124.value: 木星磁层-电离层系统周期扰动的全球图像及机理

17309124.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309124.value: Jupiter proudly showcases the most powerful auroras within our solar system, primarily energized by the rotational forces of the planet. The intricacies of these awe-inspiring auroras provide profound insights into planetary environments, in turn, serving as valuable guides for shaping the blueprints of future planetary missions and the exploration of exoplanets. Despite decades of vigilant observations of auroral emissions on giant planets, the exact physical mechanisms underpinning these radiant displays remain cloaked in mystery. The dynamics of these remarkable auroras span various temporal and spatial scales, intricately interwoven with the magnetic field dynamics of the gas giant. These dynamic processes within the auroras and the magnetosphere are the product of a constant circulation of mass and energy within the Jovian system. The periodic pulsations detected through an array of instruments in recent decades hold the promise of unveiling the inherent nature of the planetary system, offering a unique opportunity to fathom the fundamental energy processes at play. As we embark on the forthcoming project we propose, our primary goal is to craft a comprehensive overview of the periodic disturbances within Jupiter's magnetosphere-ionosphere system, ultimately laying bare the potential driving mechanisms behind these enigmatic phenomena. We anticipate that the outcomes of this endeavour will significantly advance our understanding of the pulsating energy dynamics within the Jovian system. This newfound knowledge may, in turn, have far-reaching implications for comprehending other planetary systems, including those beyond our solar system, where pulsating emissions are widely identified. 高速旋轉的木星磁場對磁層粒子進行加速，使得木星擁有太陽系最強的極光輻射。這些極光現象可以反映複雜的行星環境，因此對於未來的行星/系外行星探測任務有重要的啟示。儘管巨行星極光已經被研究了數十年，其驅動機制仍存在許多困難。 極光過程是跨越多時空尺度的現象，並與行星磁場有著複雜的關係，也是行星空間物質能量輸運的自然結果。而週期性的空間擾動與極光現象提供了獨特的視角來理解行星系統，並且在過去數十年中幫助我們獲取了行星系統的重要資訊。 本研究項目，我們計劃對木星的磁層-電離層系統的週期訊號進行系統分析，並透過分析週期資訊來理解背後對應的物理機制。我們預期本研究計畫的結果能顯著改善我們對木星週期訊號對應的能量過程的認識，並將獲得的認識應用於其他脈衝系統的研究，譬如太陽系外天體環境。

17309224.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309224.value: 木星遠磁尾的內部和外部控制因素

17309224.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309224.value: Magnetotails serve as critical regions that facilitate the exchange of mass, momentum, and energy between planetary systems and their space environments, connecting planetary atmospheres with outer space. These regions are essential not only in space plasma physics research but also in missions related to terrestrial and planetary space exploration. Nevertheless, despite the growing number of missions to and flybys of Jupiter, the deep magnetotail of this planet continues to pose a substantial challenge to current theoretical frameworks. It displays unexpected configurations with remarkably extensive extensions beyond the orbit of Saturn, not observed in the terrestrial magnetosphere. Currently, the control of the global-scale patterns and the space extension of the Jovian magnetotail remains unknown. More specifically, it is unclear what controls the configuration of the Jovian deep magnetotail and where the Jovian magnetotail ends. The answers to these questions will not only deepen our understanding of fundamental planetary processes but also have potential applications in future outer solar planetary mission developments. To address these issues, we will utilize high-resolution, three-dimensional supercomputer simulations for solar wind-Jovian magnetosphere-ionosphere interactions. The simulations will quantify the external and internal control of the deep magnetotail of Jupiter and may have potential applications to other planets such as Saturn and Uranus. This project also aims to develop a quantitative framework that includes high-order factors such as mass loading and ionospheric conductance, which will be applicable to studying deep magnetotail structures for Jupiter-like planets. Furthermore, this generalized description of fundamental planetary magnetotail physics, validated by observations published in the literature, can be applied to exoplanetary systems. In light of past successes on simulating the Jovian magnetosphere and based on our previous experience in analyzing global magnetosphere simulation data, we propose the following research activities/objectives, in order to provide new knowledge of the relationship between external/internal factors and the corresponding deep magnetotail processes, including: 1. Perform numerical simulations of high-resolution global Jovian magnetosphere simulations with different: 1) solar wind speeds; 2) interplanetary magnetic fields; 2. Perform numerical experiments of high-resolution global simulations with internal controlling factors: 1) planetary rotation speed; 2) strength of planetary dipole field; 3. Perform numerical experiments of high-resolution global simulations with other internal controlling factors: 1) mass loading from Io; 2) ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling; 4. Provide quantitative knowledge of the relationship between the external/internal factors and the Jovian deep magnetotail; derive quantitative predictions of other planetary magnetotails such as Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and/or exoplanets. 磁尾是重要的行星空間區域，行星繫統和它們的空間環境之間進行質量、動量和能量交換，將行星大氣與外太空連接起來。這些區域不僅在空間等離子物理研究中至關重要，也在與地球和行星空間探索相關的任務中起着重要作用。儘管前往木星的任務和飛掠次數不斷增加，但木星的遠磁尾仍然對當前理論框架構成重大挑戰。目前已知木星的磁尾甚至超出土星軌道的範圍。但是木星磁尾的全球模式和空間範圍仍然未知。更具體地説，目前不清楚木星遠磁尾結構以及木星磁尾的結束位置的控製因素。這些問題的答案不僅將深化我們對行星空間環境基本過程的理解，而且還可能在未來的外太陽繫行星任務開髮中具有潛在應用。爲了解決這些問題，我們將利用高分辨率、三維超級計算機模擬太陽風-木星磁層-電離層相互作用。模擬將量化外部和內部驅動因素對木星遠磁尾的控製，結果可以在其他行星如土星和天王星的研究中産生潛在應用。該項目將開髮一個包括質量加載和電離層電導率等高階因素的在內的理論框架，可用於研究類木星行星的遠磁尾結構。

17309824.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309824.value: 從機器學習的視角重啓一些經典優化算法

17309824.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309824.value: Optimization plays a foundational role in advancing contemporary technologies arising in the big-data era, ranging from machine learning, cloud computing, quantum computing, and scientific computing, to artificial intelligence generated content. To tackle such applications practically, often only first-order optimization algorithms are considered mainly because of the lack of second-order derivative information and the real-time requirement on the solvers. It is even more common for only part of the gradient information is available or computable, and thus only stochastic versions of basic optimization algorithms become implementable. The mutually inspiring interaction between optimization and machine learning poses many interesting mathematical challenges from both theoretical and numerical perspectives. In particular, there is an urgent need to design new implementable and efficient algorithms for newly emerging machine learning applications, and to establish rigorous theory to interpret why these algorithms work for certain machine learning applications. In this project, we aim to reboot some classic optimization algorithms through the lens of machine learning, and develop a new series of algorithms that are particularly customized for various fundamental machine learning applications. These algorithms are expected to be more efficient and implementable than the state-of-the-art algorithms in the literature, and they can be applied to a wider range of machine learning applications. We also aim to establish completely new theoretical assertions for these new algorithms, by which some well-known theoretical results in the literature can be significantly improved or extended. With the completion of this project, we seek to pave a new avenue for designing efficient machine-learning-friendly algorithms and thus empower the optimization toolbox for solving contemporary challenging machine learning problems, enhance the mathematical understanding of how some popular algorithms should be used in the machine learning area, and discover interesting theory that can better interpret the unknown mechanism of some existing machine learning technologies. 最優化對推動大數據時代出現的很多現代技術都起著關鍵的作用； 這些現代技術包括機器學習、雲計算、量子計算、科學計算和人工智能生成内容等等。在解決這些實際問題時，由於缺乏二階導數的信息以及對解的實時性要求，通常來説，一階優化算法用得比較多。而更常見的情況是可能只有部分梯度信息可用或者可計算；對此甚至只有一些基本的隨機優化算法才能實現。由於最優化與機器學習兩個學科相互啓發性的互動，在理論和數值兩方面都出現了很多有意思的數學挑戰。一個迫切需要解決的問題是如何為新興的機器學習問題設計高效並易實現的新算法，並從理論上嚴格解釋合理性。 本項目旨在從機器學習的視角重新審視一些經典的優化算法，並特別定制一系列適用於一些基礎機器學習問題的新算法。這些算法預計比文獻中現有的算法更高效、更易實現，並有更廣的適用性。我們還將建立一些新的理論知識用於分析這些新算法，並顯著提升或者推廣一些文獻中熟知的理論結論。 通過完成本項目，我們希望可以提供一條新的思路用於設計針對機器學習問題有效的算法從而增强解決機器學習問題的現有優化工具箱，也希望對怎麽樣在機器學習領域使用一些常用算法提供一些數學理解，並發現一些新的理論用於更好地解釋一些現有機器學習技術的未知原理。

17310024.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310024.value: 帶協變量的半參數非負張量分解

17310124.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310124.value: 大規模(分佈)魯棒優化的單循環一階演算法

17310124.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310124.value: 現實生產實踐中的許多決策問題都需要轉換成優化問題。這些優化問題的結構往往與輸入參數的密切相關。為了做出決策，決策者需要提前給出優化問題模型中的參數。而不幸的是，在大多數情況下，部分參數是不確定的且無法準確知道。近年來，魯棒優化（Robust Optimization, RO）和分布式魯棒優化（Distributionally Robust Optimization, DRO）逐漸成為考慮不確定性參數情況下決策問題的流行方法。儘管RO與DRO具有廣泛的應用背景，但它們的計算方法有限，已有的算法不能滿足現代用戶的需求。這是因為在實際應用中，決策者經常需要解決複雜的高維RO與DRO問題，這些問題可能含有大量複雜結構的約束函數。 在本項目中，申請人與合作者Daniel Kuhn教授擬開發用於求解RO與DRO的新型一階算法。注意到現有求解RO和DRO問題的一階算法大部分為雙層設計，需要非精確求解一些特定的子問題，這使得其在理論和實踐上效率都較低，且難以調整其算法參數。相比之下，本項目擬設計單層的迭代算法，即每步迭代僅涉及基於（次）梯度和投影算子的簡單閉式更新，而不包含任何外部迭代算法或複雜的子問題。本項目旨在提出的算法不僅可以有效地利用有用的問題結構，而且還允許我們輕鬆地結合隨機化技術來進一步提高算法的效率與可擴展性。該項目的預期貢獻有三方面：首先，將設計出用於解決大規模RO與DRO問題的有效算法。然後，將建立所提算法的各種理論性質，包括迭代複雜性與統計性質保證。最後，將使用合成數據集和真實數據集對所提出的RO與DRO算法進行全面的數值研究，以描述其優勢。

17310324.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310324.value: 活性多面粒子（APPs）：非均向膠體相互作用與動態組裝

17310324.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310324.value: The packing of polyhedra (e.g., tetrahedra and octahedra) in 2D/3D space not only presents intriguing math puzzles, but also holds significant implications for making advanced materials. Specifically, the packing and self-assembly of polyhedral nano- and microscale colloidal particles into various shape-dependent superstructures have led to functional materials with plasmonic, photonic, and optoelectronic properties. Most commonly, the assembly of these particles relies on entropy or short-range interactions, giving rise to materials that are in the thermodynamic equilibrium state. The objective of this project is to introduce a distinct type of polyhedral colloidal particles, termed Active Polyhedral Particles (or APPs), which are “active” due to their ability to self-propel and the tendency to interact through long-range dynamic forces. By studying the individual and collective behaviour of APPs, we aim to understand how polyhedral shapes and self-propulsion are coupled to manifest anisotropic interactions and dynamic assembly of discrete and extended superstructures. Besides deriving fundamental principles, the ultimate goal is to create non-equilibrium and reconfigurable materials that are otherwise impossible . The proposed colloidal APP systems will be constructed by subjecting polyhedral microcrystals of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to AC electric fields. By selecting proper polyhedral shapes, the field-induced colloidal propulsion and its electrokinetic mechanism will be evaluated. Next, the collective organization of APPs will be investigated at different particle concentrations and field parameters. Preliminarily, we have observed a diverse range of dynamic assemblies unique to APPs, including chiral dimers, zig-zag chains, swarms, crystals, and colloidal waves. Elucidating the characteristics and formation mechanisms of these superstructures, where polyhedral shapes interplay with activity-induced anisotropic interactions play a crucial role, is our key objective. Finally, we will explore the potentials of APP assemblies as functional materials by leveraging the composition and functionality of the MOF particles. With APPs, this project introduces a fundamentally new approach to assemble polyhedral particles, combining anisotropic shape and motion activity to drive distinct pathways for colloidal interactions and superstructures. The special characteristics of the APP system, along with the exciting preliminary observations, ensure the success and significance of this project. 多面體（例如四面體和八面體）在二維/三維空間中的堆積不僅呈現了有趣的數學難題，還對製備先進材料具有重要意義。具體來說，多面體納米和微米尺度膠體顆粒的堆積和自組裝形成了各種形狀相關的超結構，導致具有等離子、光子和光電性能的功能材料。通常情況下，這些顆粒的組裝依賴於熵或短程相互作用，形成處於熱力學平衡狀態的材料。該項目的目標是引入一種獨特類型的多面體膠體顆粒，稱為“活性多面體顆粒”（或APPs），由於其具有自主推進的能力以及通過長程動態力相互作用的傾向，因此它們是“活躍”的。通過研究APPs的個體和集體行為，我們旨在了解多面體形狀和自主推進如何耦合以表現非均向相互作用和離散和擴展超結構的動態組裝。除了推導基本原則外，最終目標是創建非平衡和可重構的材料，這在其他情況下是不可能的。擬議的膠體APP系統將通過將金屬-有機框架（MOFs）的多面體微晶置於交流電場中來構建。通過選擇適當的多面體形狀，將評估場誘導的膠體推進及其電動力學機制。接下來，將在不同顆粒濃度和場參數下研究APPs的集體組織。初步觀察到APPs獨特的一系列動態組裝，包括手性二聚體、鋸齒鏈、群集、晶體和膠體波。闡明這些超結構的特徵和形成機制，其中多面體形狀與活動誘導的非均向相互作用起著關鍵作用，是我們的主要目標。最後，我們將通過利用MOF顆粒的組成和功能，探索APP組裝作為功能材料的潛力。通過APPs，該項目引入了一種根本新的方法來組裝多面體顆粒，結合非均向形狀和運動活性，為膠體相互作用和超結構的不同路徑提供驅動。APP系統的特殊特性，以及令人興奮的初步觀察結果，確保了該項目的成功和重要性。

17310624.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17310624.value: 實現完全溶液加工的有機/鈣鈦礦光電器件的四元穩定性的雙相凝膠基低溫金屬電極

17310624.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17310624.value: 電極是新興有機/鈣鈦礦光電器件（OED）（例如發光二極體（LED）和太陽能電池（SC））中的基本電荷注入/提取組件。由液體前驅體沉積的溶液處理電極（SPE）不僅可以透過熱/電子束蒸發和濺射作為傳統電極的低成本、低碳足跡和可擴展的替代品，而且還推動了捲繞電極的新興時代。金屬奈米材料、導電聚合物和碳基材料已被探索為 SPE。包括奈米線 (AgNW) 和奈米粒子 (AgNP) 在內的銀奈米材料 (AgNM) 因其在實現優異的導電性、光澤度和機械延展性方面的可行性而成為有前途的 SPE。 由於典型的AgNM 被絕緣配體覆蓋，因此在透過溶液製程形成AgNM 薄膜後，需要進行後處理（例如熱退火(>150°C)、化學處理和曝光）以去除周圍的配體並互連鄰的AgNM。然而，前驅溶液可以滲透到其他層中，之後溶劑和後處理可能會損壞多層裝置結構（例如有機/鈣鈦礦層和柔性基板），從而降低裝置性能。由於後處理不完善而導致相鄰 AgNM 之間的晶格不匹配也會削弱電氣性能。同時，AgNM 的幾何依賴型等離子體效應會導致強烈的光散射和吸收，從而導致光學損失。最後，周圍環境、熱、機械力和電偏置條件是電極普遍關注的問題，影響四元化學-熱-電-機械穩定性。因此，同時最大限度地減少溶劑和後處理的影響、抑制光學損失、了解晶體生長機制並提高基於 AgNM 的 SPE 的穩定性非常重要。 我們將首先開發一種用於基於 AgNW 的 SPE 的室溫低溶劑參與雙相凝膠燒結技術，以解決溶劑和後處理問題。我們還將研究凝膠條件下的 AgNM 生長/燒結機制，以實現高品質的 SPE。接下來，我們將操縱 AgNW 的幾何形狀和配體來減少 SPE 中的光學損耗，並展示其針對不同應用的可調透射率/反射率。關於四元穩定性，我們提出了一種低溫雙錨定策略，其中引入協同相互作用網絡與Ag表面配位，然後透過層層相互作用建立互連聚合物結構以進一步穩定係統。最後，我們將整合已開發的方法來展示全解決方案處理的 OED，包括 SC 和 LED 陣列。這項工作不僅有助於建立晶體生長/燒結的新知識和設計基於金屬奈米材料的SPE，實現優異的光電性能和四元穩定性，而且還有助於開發用於實際應用的低成本溶液加工OED。

17311224.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17311224.value: 發光金屬-配體配位化合物的設計與合成及其作為構築塊在分節多嵌段金屬超分子的共組裝

17311224.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17311224.value: The precise control of linking different atoms or molecular components together in a desirable spatial arrangement and order has always been a challenging task in synthesis. In molecular synthesis, the linking of atoms and molecular components will involve the formation of chemical bonds, mainly dominated by covalent bond formation. The parallel precise control of assembly of molecules in a highly-ordered, directional and spatially organized fashion is still at its infancy. In particular, the precise control of assembly of multi-component systems via supramolecular noncovalent interactions rather than covalent bonding via chemical ligation has attracted much attention. One major challenge involves the controlled segmental growth of multi-block co-assemblies with micron dimensions, which is no simple task especially for those based on metal-ligand coordination complexes as building blocks. Even more challenging is to achieve well-controlled segmented growth of multi-blocks involving flexible blocks at the termini. Thus there is an urgent need for discovering new varieties of alternative strategies for the construction of segmented multi-blocks and the precise control of their order other than decorations only at the active termini of the block. In this project, unlike typical seeded supramolecular growth that usually involves a single-component system or more recently, two-component system with the two components being structurally very similar, we will explore the use of two- or more component system with structurally dissimilar components, especially pre-formed single-component metallosupramolecular self-assemblies as the precursor for the two- to multi-component supramolecular co-assembly with block copolymers. The spectroscopic, electronic absorption, luminescence, co-assembly and morphological properties of the metal-ligand coordination complexes and their metallosupramolecular co-assemblies will be studied. A systematic study and understanding of the control of assembly/co-assembly, their assembly/co-assembly mechanisms and associated thermodynamics and kinetics will lead to important information and insights governing the future design of multi-block copolymer systems with controlled morphologies and chromophoric and luminescence properties. These metal complex building blocks capable of displaying non-covalent metal-metal interactions with distinctive color and luminescence properties will be able to provide a versatile platform to monitor the segmental growth of multi-component metallosupramolecular copolymer systems. It is envisaged that the proposed strategy will provide insights and guiding principles for controlled on-demand site-specific supramolecular co-assembly between metal complex monomers/unimers self-assembled supramolecular polymers and block copolymers to give tri- and multi-block metallosupramolecular copolymer systems. 在合成過程中，精準控制不同的原子和分子的連接及空間排列是極具挑戰性的任務。原子和分子在合成時會產生化學鍵，通常以共價鍵為主。目前通過高度有序、定向和空間組織的方法來精準控制分子組裝的研究仍處於起步階段，而通過超分子非共價相互作用來精準控制多元分子系統的組裝亦引起了廣泛關注。其中一個主要挑戰是微米多嵌段共組裝體的可控分段生長，這對基於金屬-配體配位化合物作為構築塊的系統尤其困難；叧外，精準控制具柔性塊在末端的多嵌段共組裝體的分段生長也是一項具挑戰性的工作。因此，迫切需要研究新的策略來構建分節的多嵌段共組裝體及精準控制其順序，而非僅僅修飾構築塊末端。與典型的單元分子系統或結構相似的二元分子系統的超分子生長不同，本項目將探索具不同結構的二元或多元分子系統的超分子生長，包括利用單元系統金屬超分子自組裝體作前驅體及嵌段共聚物來構建二元和多元超分子共組裝。此外，本項目將研究金屬-配體配位化合物及其金屬超分子共組裝體的光譜、電子吸收、發光、共組裝及形態性質，並會對組裝/共組裝的控制、其機理及相關的熱力學和動力學進行研究和理解，研究成果將為未來設計具可控形態、發色和發光性質的多嵌段共聚物系統提供重要資訊和見解。這些金屬配合物構築塊將展示具有獨特顏色和發光性質的非共價金屬-金屬相互作用，從而提供一個多功能平台來監測多元金屬超分子共聚物系統的分段生長。本項目研究的嶄新策略將為金屬配合物單體/單聚體自組裝超分子聚合物和共聚物之間的可控按需位點特異性超分子共組裝提供見解和指導原則，從而研發三元和多元金屬超分子共聚物系統。

17500224.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500224.value: 減弱共享經濟中專業與非專業賣家之間的不平等問題

17500224.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17500224.value: Dr Feng, Yu Prof Shen, Qiaowei

17500224.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500224.value: Peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms—or the “sharing economy”—have become increasingly popular. Their peer-to-peer nature facilitates direct connections between individuals and allows nonprofessionals to leverage underutilized resources. However, the P2P nature has been diluted in recent years due to a rise in professional players joining the P2P platforms, or the so-called “professionalism” issue. These professional sellers can potentially hurt the profits of nonprofessional sellers, crowd out nonprofessionals, and harm platform growth. The professionalism issue has also attracted government scrutiny, resulting in regulations on P2P platforms. For example, cities have implemented regulations on Airbnb (e.g., occupancy tax and capping the number of listings per host) due to concerns that short-term rentals owned by full-time professional investors have negatively impacted public school enrollments and housing shortages. Despite the importance of addressing professionalism in the sharing economy, academic literature on this topic is scant due to limited data and empirical opportunities. This study aims to fill this gap by analyzing a natural experiment on a major secondhand P2P platform (Zhuanzhuan) in China. The platform introduced a submarket called “YanXuan” in May 2020, which standardizes and facilitates the selling process. This new market could potentially help nonprofessional sellers overcome their sales expertise and performance disadvantages compared with professional sellers. We examine the following research questions: (1) What are the effects of YanXuan adoption on listing sales and seller revenues? (2) What is the differential impact of adoption on professional and nonprofessional sellers? (3) Does YanXuan help reduce the professional-nonprofessional gap? and (4) Do sellers respond to YanXuan by adjusting their pricing, quality, service provision, and information disclosure strategies? We will adopt a difference-in-difference framework by analyzing listing-level and seller-level outcomes before and after YanXuan adoption. Sellers choose whether and when to adopt the YanXuan market. We will use econometrics methods (e.g., inverse probability of treatment weighting) to address the nonrandomness of the treatment assignment due to sellers’ self-selection issue. Our research has important implications for P2P platforms and policymakers. Our findings will help platforms understand the effectiveness of platform interventions on the professional-nonprofessional gap and the differential impacts on heterogeneous seller groups. For policymakers who launch various regulations to constrain professional players, our research offers an alternative approach to addressing the professionalism issue by assisting nonprofessional players. Policymakers can use our findings to understand the impact of alternative approaches on sellers, buyers, and P2P platforms. 點對點（P2P）平台或所謂的“共享經濟”已經越來越受到歡迎。它們的點對點特性促進了個人之間的直接連接，並允許非專業人士利用未充分利用的資源。然而，近年來由於專業賣家加入P2P平台，或者所謂的“專業化”問題，P2P的性質已經被稀釋。這些專業賣家可能會損害非專業賣家的利潤，擠出非專業人士，並損害平台的增長。專業化問題也引起了政府的關注，導致對P2P平台的規範。例如，由於擔心全職專業投資者擁有的短期租賃對公共學校入學率和住房短缺造成了負面影響，一些城市對Airbnb實施了規範（例如住宿稅和限制每個房東的房源數量）。儘管解決共享經濟中的專業化問題非常重要，但由於數據和實證研究機會有限，學術文獻對此主題的研究非常稀缺。本研究旨在通過分析中國一個主要的二手P2P平台（轉轉）上的自然實驗來填補這一空白。該平台在2020年5月推出了一個名為“嚴選”的子市場，平台在其中規範並便利了銷售過程。這個新市場可能有助於非專業賣家克服他們與專業賣家相比的銷售專業知識和績效劣勢。我們將研究以下問題：（1）嚴選市場對商品銷售和賣家收入的影響是什麼？（2）嚴選市場對專業和非專業賣家的差異性影響是什麼？（3）嚴選是否有助於縮小專業與非專業賣家之間的差距？（4）賣家是否會通過調整他們的定價、商品質量、服務提供和信息披露等策略來回應嚴選市場的引入。我們將採用雙重差分法(difference-in-difference)分析嚴選市場引入前後商品銷售和賣家收入的變化。由於賣家可以自主選擇是否及何時採用嚴選市場，我們將使用計量經濟學方法（例如，逆概率處理加權inverse probability of treatment weighting）來解決因賣家自主選擇問題而導致的試驗分派的非隨機性。我們的研究對P2P平台和政策制定者具有重要意義。我們的發現將幫助平台了解平台干預對專業與非專業賣家之間差距的影響和對異質賣家群體的不同影響。對於以往通過限制專業買家來解決專業化問題的政策制定者，我們的研究提供了一種通過幫助非專業買家來解決專業化問題的新方案。政策制定者可以使用我們的研究結果來了解該方案對賣家，買家和P2P平台的影響。

17500524.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500524.value: 取决于参照物的偏好和资产定价

17500524.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17500524.value: Prof Benhabib, Jess Prof Wang, Pengfei

17500524.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500524.value: The excess volatility puzzle is one of the most significant findings in financial economics. As first identified by Shiller (1981) and Leroy and Porter (1981), stock prices fluctuate much more than fundamentals (dividends or earnings). The phenomenon of excess volatility is particularly prominent during economic downturns. Financial industrial participants and academic researchers have long argued that investor expectations can play a large role in driving excess fluctuations in asset prices. Notably, Keynes (1936, ch. 12) discusses at length the "animal spirits" nature of the stock market, emphasizing that the market can be subject to waves of optimistic and pessimistic sentiment. In this proposed project, we pose a basic question. Can investors' expectations, which are driven by some non-fundamentals, lead to fluctuations in asset prices within a standard general-equilibrium asset pricing framework? Our preliminary theoretical result shows that the existence of non-fundamental equilibria is impossible in an expected-utility based standard rational expectations model of asset pricing. However, once a behavioral assumption --- reference-dependent preferences as developed by Kahneman and Tversky (1979) and Koszegi and Rabin (2006, 2007) --- is introduced, non-fundamental equilibrium emerges and resolves some of the empirical puzzles. In this proposed project, we will first develop our preliminary theoretical result to construct a full-fledged theoretical model suitable for quantitative calibration, and then conduct calibration by confronting the model with data. 超额波动之谜是金融经济学最重要的发现之一。正如 Shiller（1981 年）以及 Leroy 和 Porter（1981 年）首次发现的那样，股票价格的波动远大于基本面（股息或收益）的波动。过度波动现象在经济衰退时期尤为突出。金融业参与者和学术研究人员长期以来一直认为，投资者的预期在推动资产价格过度波动方面起着很大作用。值得注意的是，凯恩斯（1936 年，第 12 章）详细讨论了股票市场的 “动物精神 ”特性，强调市场会受到乐观和悲观情绪的波及。在本拟议项目中，我们提出了一个基本问题。在标准的一般均衡资产定价框架内，投资者受某些非基本因素驱动的预期能否导致资产价格的波动？我们的初步理论结果表明，在基于预期效用的标准理性预期资产定价模型中，不可能存在非基本面均衡。然而，一旦引入行为假设--由 Kahneman 和 Tversky（1979 年）以及 Koszegi 和 Rabin（2006 年、2007 年）提出的依赖参考的偏好--非基本面均衡就会出现，并解决一些经验性难题。在本拟议项目中，我们将首先发展我们的初步理论成果，构建一个适合定量校准的完整理论模型，然后通过模型与数据的对抗进行校准。

17501324.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501324.value: 贸易协定，全球供应链，与跨国公司

17501324.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17501324.value: Dr De Souza, Gustavo Prof Tang, Heiwai

17501324.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501324.value: （深度）贸易协定如何影响企业在全球供应链中的国际采购和出口？贸易协定是否为跨国公司提供比国内公司更多的利益，如果是，那么是通过哪些机制？我们的目标是利用一份新建立的、关于全球企业双边贸易和金融信息的数据库以及一个关于跨国公司和全球供应链的定量模型，率先解决这些问题。 利用Panjiva数据，我们评估贸易协定对企业双边贸易关系的影响以及这种影响如何根据企业和贸易关系特征而变化。此外，我们还研究了贸易协定对第三国企业的溢出效应。通过将Panjiva数据与Orbis数据匹配，我们探讨了跨国公司是否因贸易协定而胜过国内公司，以及有助于跨国企业优势的机制。 为了可靠地研究这些影响，我们采用了双重差分法的估计策略，并通过签署贸易协定引入了变化。根据这些实证估计，我们开发并校准了一个关于跨国公司和全球供应链的模型，以分析贸易协定对本地和全球福利的影响。

17501824.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501824.value: 相对绩效考核与员工招募

Examine whether and how the use of relative performance evaluation (RPE) affects the focal firms' inclination to poach peer firms' employees. Investigate whether the effect varies with peer characteristics that affect the incentives of sabotaging/collusion Investigate whether the effect varies with market structure that affects the cost/benefit of sabotaging/collusion Investigate whether the effect varies with employee characteristics. 17501824.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501824.value: 本项目旨在研究相对绩效评估（RPE）的运用如何对劳动力市场竞争产生影响。基于相对绩效评估的薪酬制度已在众多公司中得到广泛应用。例如，目前超过三分之二的标普500公司采用了该评估方式。尽管理论上相对绩效评估有助于在高管和股东之间有效地分担风险，但学界和业界对其可能产生的意外后果表示担忧。具体而言，该评估可能会鼓励企业采取手段破坏对手的绩效，或者与对手达成勾结协议。然而，由于缺乏关于公司之间随时间变化的战略互动的详细信息，目前实证文献关于相对绩效评估对公司间战略互动影响的研究相对匮乏。为了应对这一挑战，我们将通过追溯员工职业生涯的详细信息以识别公司间的劳动力流动，并制定衡量员工挖角的指标。 具体而言，我们将探讨相对绩效评估如何影响一个公司招募对手公司员工的意愿，这在理论上尚不明确。一方面，“破坏性竞争”假设预测相对绩效评估将激励公司招募对手员工以提高公司的相对绩效，这是因为员工挖角有助于其（i）吸引人才，同时削弱对手的人力资本和（ii）获取关于对手的关键知识。另一方面，“合谋”假设则预测相反的效果。 基于2009-2020年期间的公司-竞争对手-年度面板数据，我们计划使用面板回归和双重差分法回归来研究在将对手纳入公司的相对绩效评估标杆企业组之后，劳动力由对手流向公司的变化。我们将控制公司-年度固定效应和竞争对手-年度固定效应，以控制公司劳动力需求冲击和对手公司劳动力需求冲击（例如裁员）。我们还将采用多种策略来解决内生性问题，并探讨基于市场结构（例如战略互补品与替代品）、对手特征（例如相对中期业绩）和员工特征（例如职位排名和技能）的横截面差异，以揭示潜在的机制。 总之，本研究旨在丰富关于相对绩效评估对公司间战略互动产生的实际经济后果的讨论。通过深入探讨这一问题，我们希望能为业界和政策制定者提供关于激励机制、竞争策略和劳动力市场发展的实用建议。我们的研究将有助于解释和预测相对绩效评估在劳动力市场竞争中的影响，为公司制定更有效的人才招聘和激励政策提供依据。

17501824.label: Realisation of objectives
17501824.value: Regarding 1: We leverage granular resume data (12.5 million entries) to identify the employee flows between industry rivals over the 2009-2019 period. Our final sample consists of 199,377 focal firm-rival-year observations, covering 1,113 (4,359) unique focal firms (rivals) with 198,991 poaching cases Regarding 2: We construct a firm-rival-year panel, and regress the incidence of employee poaching on the indicator of rival inclusion in RPE, controlling for pair fixed effects and year fixed effects. We document a positive and significant association between RPE peer status and employee flow from rival to focal firm. Regarding 3-5: We conduct cross-sectional tests based on employee skills, employee work experience in rival firms, the importance of RPE to CEO compensation, the performance metrics used in RPE contracts. We find that RPE-induced poaching is more prevalent among hard-to-replace workers, when RPE is more important to CEO compensation, and when RPE contracts are based on accounting measures. Regarding 6: We study the impact of RPE, along with successful poaching, on rivals' labor input costs. We find that RPE-induced poaching increase the costs of labor as the input in rival's production function.

17501824.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501824.value: In this study, we empirically examine this prediction through the lens of firms’ employee poaching practices. By leveraging detailed data on employee movements across firms, we present consistent evidence to suggest that RPE incentives drive executives to actively poach employees away from their RPE peers. Specifically, within a firm-rival pair, the inclusion of the rival as an RPE peer is associated with an economically and statistically significant ∼3 percentage point increase in employee inflow from the rival to the focal firm, at the extensive margin. Additionally, we find that focal firms tend to target valuable, hard-to-replace employees (i.e., skilled individuals with longer tenures) from their RPE peers. These effects are more pronounced when the RPE plan is based on accounting metrics and when the proportion of executives’ total performance-pay grants derived from RPE grants is greater. Overall, our results suggest that the use of RPE in CEO pay plans encourages managers to poach valuable employees away from their RPE peers to harm the peers and thus boost their relative performance. We further provide descriptive evidence which suggests that this tactic is costly to the RPE peers. Companies that are used as RPE peers by others face heightened competition for their own labor talent, and thus labor appears to become a more expensive input in their production process.

17501824.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501824.value: Future research should explore how rival firms respond to talent poaching, including whether they retaliate with reciprocal hiring or improve labor policies to retain workers. Examining these dynamics can reveal whether poaching triggers competitive wage spirals, enhances worker welfare, or leads to inefficient labor market outcomes. A key empirical challenge is disentangling strategic reactions from broader labor market trends. To address this, studies could exploit exogenous shocks—such as sudden regulatory changes, non-compete clause enforcements, or unexpected competitor expansions—that exogenously shift poaching incentives. By analyzing how peer firms adjust hiring, compensation, and retention strategies following such shocks, researchers could better identify causal effects. Additionally, future work should assess the broader welfare implications for workers, including mobility patterns, wage growth, and job stability. A quasi-experimental approach would strengthen empirical identification, providing clearer insights into labor market competition and firm-level strategic behavior.

17501824.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501824.value: Our study contributes to the literature on the link between competition and the use of relative performance evaluation in executive compensation plans. Specifically, we provide new evidence that RPE incentives push executives to poach labor market talent away from their RPE peers, seemingly as a means of harming those companies. In this regard, our study contributes to the growing literature on the intersection of labor and finance by documenting the effect of executive compensation practices on labor talent acquisition. Firms can build human capital in different ways and recent studies have examined how the acquisition and retention of human capital impact: (i) firms’ choices to grow internally or through M&As; along with (ii) the outcomes of M&As. In this paper, we consider how executives’ compensation incentives factor into firms’ labor talent acquisition decisions, showing that RPE pushes firms to poach hard-to-replace rank-and-file employees from their peers.
