26208924.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26208924.value: 针对开放多模态数据理解的多模态事件关系图的构建

26208924.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26208924.value: 事件是我们现实世界和日常变化的基本组成元素。一些事件可能“很复杂”，并且可以从多个角度或者不同模态来描述。例如，对于一个父事件“北京2022冬季奥运会”，就有来自不同记者的大量视频或新闻文章。所谓“父事件”，我们的意思是这个事件由多个子事件（即子事件）组成，如“开幕式”。因此，理解所有事件元素和子事件如何逻辑上连接对于理解整个复杂事件至关重要。 尽管自然语言处理领域有大量关于文本事件研究的研究，但视觉事件研究仍然落后。例如，视觉社区专注于使用封闭集词汇提取图像或视频事件。最近的工作开始检测一些类型的视频事件-事件关系。在多模态学习中，他们只关注共指事件关系（又称，视觉锚定）。因此，所有现有的工作都无法处理多模态数据，并理解复杂的多模态事件-事件关系。 在本项目中，我们提出了第一个从多模态数据输入生成多模态事件关系图的框架。具体来说，我们同时解决三个关键挑战：1）输入的多模态资产包括来自不同形式和语义层次的事件。2）开放词汇：我们旨在以开放词汇的方式提取事件，因为手动定义日常事件中的所有候选事件类别是不切实际的。同时，我们还将现有的多模态事件-事件关系类型扩展到更全面的类别。3）弱注释：对于两个事件对，它们可能同时具有多个事件-事件关系。因此，在大型数据集中完全注释所有事件-事件关系以进行训练是不可能的。我们旨在以弱监督的方式检测所有事件-事件关系。 我们将从三个角度实现我们的目标：1）我们提出了第一个开放词汇视频事件提取方法。2）我们扩展现有的共指关系到更多类别，以识别事件-事件关系并连接所有事件。3）我们提出了一种针对事件中心任务的内存和参数高效的迁移学习机制，以从预训练模型转移开放词汇感知的知识。通过将非结构化输入转化为结构化的事件复合体，我们提出的框架增强了基于事件的下游应用的可解释性。例如，它可以帮助识别多模态错误信息检测中的蕴含或冲突事件或关系。

26210324.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26210324.value: 提升在线平台的用户满意度：结合不确定性的动态排序算法

26210324.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26210324.value: This proposal develops dynamic ranking algorithms for online platforms, specifically aimed at optimizing cumulative user satisfaction across an entire ranked list. Instead of basing rankings solely on predicted satisfaction, our approach incorporates estimation uncertainty, favoring rankings that hold the highest potential for user satisfaction. We emphasize a dynamic approach where model estimations and uncertainty quantification are continually refined as new data becomes available. Our comprehensive model takes into account varied user preferences, the diversity of items, and the nuanced impact of item positioning. This multifaceted strategy not only addresses the heterogeneity of online users and items but also taps into flexible approximation tools, drawing from both parametric functional classes and non-parametric machine learning techniques such as neural networks. Ultimately, our objective is to equip online platforms with the necessary tools to enhance their daily ranking operations. Specifically, our research focuses on: 1. Model Development: Formulate a model capturing the diverse user and item characteristics, as well as the distinct position effects of each item. 2. Efficient Optimization: Achieve optimal rankings in polynomial time by exploiting our model's structure, bypassing exhaustive enumeration. 3. Statistically-Grounded Dynamic Ranking Algorithms: Develop contextual bandit-based ranking algorithms to optimize cumulative user satisfaction with statistical guarantees on optimality. 4. Robustness Check: Conduct both empirical and theoretical sensitivity analyses, exploring model bias effects and balancing bias-variance on the top of the exploration-exploitation in the dynamic ranking. 5. Real-World Application: Partner with a major online platform to showcase the real-world efficacy of our method through A/B tests. 该提案开发了在线平台的动态排序算法，旨在优化整个排序列表中的累积用户满意度。我们的方法不仅基于预测的满意度，还结合了估计的不确定性，优先考虑那些具有最高用户满意度潜力的排序。我们强调动态方法，随着新数据的不断涌入，模型估计和不确定性量化也不断得到改进。我们的综合模型考虑了不同用户偏好、物品多样性以及物品位置的微妙影响。这种多方面的策略不仅解决了在线用户和物品的异质性问题，还利用了灵活的逼近工具，既包括参数函数类，也包括非参数机器学习模型如神经网络。最终，我们的目标是为在线平台提供必要的工具，以增强其日常排序操作。具体而言，我们的研究重点包括： 1. 模型开发：构建一个模型，捕捉多样的用户和物品特征，以及每个物品的独特位置效应。 2. 高效优化：通过利用模型的结构，以多项式时间实现最优排序，避免穷举枚举。 3. 动态排序算法：开发基于上下文的老虎机排序算法，以统计保证的最优性来优化累积用户满意度。 4. 稳健性检查：进行实证和理论的敏感性分析，探讨模型偏差效应，并在动态排序中的探索-利用权衡基础上平衡偏差-方差。 5. 真实世界应用：与一个主要在线平台合作，通过在线对照试验展示我们方法的实际效果。

26215824.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26215824.value: 賦能太空連續纖維增材製造的動態軌跡和力控制

26215824.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26215824.value: In the history of human space exploration, in-space manufacturing is identified as a revolutionary milestone as it enables on-demand manufacturing capabilities with bulk, recycled, and space-mined materials, laying the foundation for long-endurance, commercially viable, and self-sufficient space missions. Currently, in-space additive manufacturing is the primary trend, and people have successfully printed in orbit using the fused filament fabrication method with various thermoplastics. Continuous-fiber additive manufacturing (CFAM) is highlighted as a promising future in-space manufacturing solution for fabricating lightweight, high-stiffness, high-strength, and large-scale parts. However, CFAM still faces challenges in space due to high process variability and a lack of mature fiber trajectory generation/optimization/control algorithms. This proposed research investigates the optimization and dynamic feedback control methods to address these challenges, paving the way for robust CFAM in space. Most existing CFAM processes are open-loop controlled and thus exhibit high variability under different materials, contact conditions, and gravity. Our preliminary investigations indicate that the contact force between the nozzle and the printed part and the thermal images shed light on potential closed-loop control as it contains abundant dynamic information. However, there is a lack of fundamental understanding of the dynamic connections between the contact force and the printing conditions. To fill this gap, this project proposed a hybrid modeling framework, embracing physics-based and data-driven models, to quantitively establish the dynamic model that the contact force reflects the printing conditions, under different gravity. Building on the model, the project aims to construct the first real-time closed-loop controlled CFAM process exploiting the contact force and thermal imaging feedback. CFAM in space requires accurate fiber path design and optimization. Current methods generate an optimized direction field and fit the fiber path; the multi-stage optimization causes uncertainties, errors, and suboptimality. To address this issue, the research proposes investigating direct manipulation of the fiber path under a B-spline framework, enabling analytical gradient with finite element models and seamless connections to the feedback control framework. Overall, the proposed research is expected to establish a new CFAM process framework that generates optimized fiber paths, senses the printing conditions in real time with the contact force and thermal imaging, and dynamically controls the speed, extrusion, and layer spacing for robust printing performances for process variations and microgravity conditions. The proposed new closed-loop high-robust CFAM process will be verified in a microgravity tower to prepare for next-step verification in orbits. 太空製造在人類太空探索歷史中具有重要意義。它可以利用原材料、回收材料和太空開採的資源進行按需製造，爲長期、商業可行且自給自足的太空任務奠定基礎。其中，連續纖維增材製造作爲一種輕量高强零部件製造方法備受關注，但在太空應用中仍面臨挑戰。主要問題在於連續纖維增材製造過程的一致性難以保證，同時缺乏成熟的軌迹生成優化和閉環控制方法。本研究旨在建立通用的纖維路徑生成方法，並利用打印過程中的力和熱信息建立動態反饋，爲不同重力環境下的太空連續纖維增材製造奠定基礎。 目前，大多數連續纖維增材過程採用開環控制。因此，在不同材料、接觸條件和重力環境下存在較大差異。初步調查顯示，噴嘴與打印零件之間的接觸力和熱像圖包含豐富的動態信息，有提供閉環控制的潛力。然而，目前對接觸力與打印條件之間的動態聯繫缺乏基本理解。爲填補這一知識空白，本項目提出了一個混合建模框架，結合基於物理和數據驅動的模型，動態地反映接觸力與打印效果在不同重力條件下的關係。基於該模型，該項目旨在實現國際首例利用接觸力和熱成像反饋的實時閉環控制的纖維增材製造過程。 此外，太空中的連續纖維增材製造需要準確的纖維路徑設計和優化。目前的方法生成優化的方向場並擬合纖維路徑，但此類多階段優化方法可能導致不確定性、誤差和次優性。爲解决這一問題，本研究提出在B樣條框架下直接操作纖維路徑，實現與有限元模型的解析梯度和與反饋控制框架的無縫連接。 總體而言，本研究旨在建立一個新的連續纖維增材製造過程框架，能夠生成優化的纖維軌迹，並在實時感知力-熱信息的基礎上調節速度、擠出和層間間距等打印參數，以實現在不同重力環境下的一致性打印表現。項目預期建立的閉環高魯棒性纖維增材製造方法將在其他重力環境中進行驗證，爲下一步在軌驗證奠定基礎。

26218024.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26218024.value: 在去中心化计算资源上的开源基础模型训练框架

26218024.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26218024.value: Over the past few years, open-source foundation models have demonstrated impressive performance and sparked a new wave of exciting AI applications. However, training these foundation models, such as OPT-175B, Llama2-70B, and Falcon-180B, can be extremely computation-intensive, often involving thousands of GPUs running continuously for months. The high cost of deploying such training tasks in a centralized cluster has become an obvious obstacle limiting the evolution of open foundation models. In this project, we propose to study how to deploy the training of open foundation models over economic, heterogeneous, and decentralized computational resources, such as spot GPU instances across different cloud providers, idled GPUs in educational HPC clusters, and gaming GPUs from volunteering individuals. Technically, we are facing two main challenges in accommodating foundation model training in such a decentralized environment when compared to the centralized data center: i) the capacity of the computational resources and inter-machine connections can be highly heterogeneous, and ii) the cross-region communications can be significantly (one or two orders of magnitude) slower than that inside a data center. To overcome these two challenges, we plan to tackle the problem through a careful co-design of the machine learning system and machine algorithm: at the system level, we will propose an effective system scheduling method to coordinate the state-of-the-art parallel training strategies, including data-, pipeline-, tensor model-, and optimizer-parallelism over heterogeneous computation capacity and network connections; at the algorithm level, we will study advanced communication-efficient algorithms that can alleviate the communication bottleneck through the cross-region slow links. Furthermore, we plan to deliver a production-level open-source software stack for our research outcomes. This proposed study provides an efficient solution that lowers the barrier of entry to train open foundation models, and we hope the democratization of this technology could spur innovation and diversity in AI applications from every possible domain. 近年来，开源基础模型表现出色，进而推动产生了新一系列令人兴奋的机遇生成式人工智能的应用产品。然而，训练这些基础模型（如OPT-175B、Llama2-70B和Falcon-180B等）需要极高的计算资源，通常需要占用数千个GPU连续数月的时间。我们认为将这些训练任务部署在集中式高性能集群中的高成本已成为限制开源基础模型演进的明显障碍。在本项目中，我们计划研究如何在经济的、异构的和去中心化的计算资源上部署开源基础模型的训练：例如跨不同云提供商的spot GPU实例、教育机构的高性能计算集群中闲置的GPU以及志愿加入计算网络的个人所属的游戏GPU。从技术上讲，与集中式数据中心相比，在这样一个去中心化的环境中进行基础模型训练面临两个主要挑战：1）计算资源和机器间连接的能力高度异质性，2）跨区域通信比数据中心内的高性能网络中的通信慢一个或两个数量级。为了克服这两项挑战，我们计划通过机器学习系统和分布式优化算法的协同设计来完成这一课题：在系统层面，我们将提出一种有效的系统调度方法，以协调数据并行、流水线并行、张量模型并行和优化器并行等最新的并行训练策略，适应异构计算能力和网络连接；在算法层面，我们将研究先进的通信高效算法，以缓解跨区域慢速链接的通信瓶颈。此外，我们计划提供一个产品级的开源软件栈来开源分享我们的研究成果。我们希望我们的研究可以提供了一种高效的分布式训练解决方案，从而降低了训练开源基础模型的入门门槛，进而使得我们研发的这种技术能够激发各个领域的AI创新。

26301724.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26301724.value: 粗略波動率的穩健推斷

26301724.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26301724.value: Capturing the dynamics of asset price volatility in a precise and timely fashion is key to risk management, asset pricing and other financial activities. The emergence of high-frequency trading over the last two decades has significantly increased the pace at which financial markets operate, with risks as well as hedging opportunities changing over much shorter time horizons. In recent years, the so-called rough volatility models have gained considerable interest in the quantitative finance literature. This class of models postulates that volatility changes more quickly and is much more irregular than traditional models would entail. Even though rough volatility is consistent with market data, criticism has been voiced recently because some data features supporting rough volatility models might result from estimation errors, price and volatility jumps, or mean-reversion of volatility. As a result, it remains a controversial question among researchers: Is volatility rough, or not? The goal of this proposal is to answer this question by developing a comprehensive package of statistical tools to estimate the roughness of volatility. We will employ novel statistical methods that overcome the latency of volatility and are robust to other confounding features of financial data such as jumps, noise, or drifts. To further enhance the robustness of our results, we will exploit two independent sets of financial data and devise a separate statistical inference program for each data set. First, using high-frequency asset return data, we will construct an estimator of volatility roughness by establishing a one-to-one link between volatility roughness and the predictability of intraday volatility estimates. Second, using a novel data set containing zero-day options (i.e., options that expire on the same day as they are traded), we will build a robust estimator of volatility roughness by analyzing the behavior of option-based volatility-related quantities as the time-to-expiry of the options approaches zero. The outcomes of this proposal will immediately benefit the academic community by settling the scholarly dispute whether volatility is rough or not. From a practical perspective, rough volatility means that volatility moves are predictable. Therefore, by shedding light into the intraday dynamics of volatility, this project will ultimately lead to better models, better estimates and better predictions in financial markets. This in turn will benefit investors, risk managers, and policy makers in an era where real-time market information has become indispensable. 準確及時地捕捉資產價格波動率是風險管理、資產定價和其他金融活動的關鍵。過去二十年高頻交易的出現明顯加快了金融市場的運行速度，導致風險和對沖機會在更短的時間內發生變化。 近年來，所謂的粗略波動率模型在計量金融文獻中引起了相當大的興趣。此類模型假設波動率比傳統模型變化更快且更不規則。儘管粗略波動率與市場數據一致，但最近也有人提出批評，因為支持粗略波動率模型的一些數據特徵可能是由統計誤差、價格和波動率跳躍或波動率均值回歸造成的。因此，這仍然是研究人員之間一個有爭議的問題：波動率是否粗略？ 該提案的目標是透過開發一套全面的統計工具來估計波動率的粗略度來回答這個問題。我們將採用新穎的統計方法來克服波動率的潛伏性，並對金融數據的其他混雜特徵（例如跳躍、雜訊或漂移）具有穩健性。為了進一步增強我們結果的穩健性，我們將利用兩組獨立的金融數據，並為每個數據集設計一個單獨的統計推斷程序。首先，使用高頻資產回報數據，我們將在波動率粗略度和日內波動率估計值的可預測性之間建立一對一的聯繫，以建立波動率粗略度的估計量。其次，使用包含零日期權（即在交易同一天到期的期權）的新穎數據集，我們將透過分析基於零日期權估計的波動率，建構一個穩健的波動率粗略度估計量。 該提案的結果將立即使學術界受益，解決波動率是否粗略的學術爭議。從實際角度來看，粗略波動率代表波表動率走勢是可以預測的。因此，透過揭示日內波動率動態特性，該專案最終將在金融市場上帶來更好的模型、更好的估計和更好的預測。在即時市場資訊變得不可或缺的時代，這有利於投資者、風險管理者和政策制定者。

26301824.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26301824.value: 随机环境下的高斯自由场水平集和随机交织的渗流与隔断

26301824.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26301824.value: Percolation theory can roughly be characterized as the study of the connectivity properties of random graphs arising from the removal of vertices (or edges) from an underlying fixed graph such as the integer lattice in dimensions greater or equal to two, according to some predescribed rule. In recent years, several percolation models with long-range, algebraically decaying correlations have been the object of intensive and ongoing study. Two important benchmark models are given by the level-sets of the (discrete) Gaussian free field and the vacant set of random interlacements. On the integer lattice in dimensions larger or equal to three, both models are known to undergo a non-trivial percolation phase transition identified by the formation of an (almost surely unique) infinite connected component, and both the existence and sharpness of this phase transition, as well as the properties of both models in their corresponding off-critical regimes have been addressed thoroughly. A question of particular interest is to understand how interfaces or macroscopic holes are created in the "(strongly) supercritical regimes" of these percolation models, that is, when the existence of an infinite connected component that consumes most of the ambient space becomes typical. The proposed project will focus on the investigation of versions of these models on the integer lattice endowed with (potentially degenerate) random weights, which may be interpreted as impurities. In a previous work, quantitative controls on a disconnection event, in which the lower level-set of the Gaussian free field isolates a macroscopic set from the boundary of an enclosing box, have been obtained in the set-up of uniformly elliptic random weights. This project will address two principal problems: Firstly, we plan to obtain a more precise understanding of the nature of the percolation phase transition in the set-up of uniformly elliptic random weights in dimensions three and higher. Secondly, we aim at establishing controls on the probability of disconnection events in the framework of random, non-elliptic environments (such as the level-sets of the Gaussian free field, or the vacant set of random interlacements, on a supercritical cluster of Bernoulli percolation) in dimensions larger or equal to three, and to study related questions in two dimensions. The results from this research project should give further insights into the role of impurities on long-range percolation models, and involve the development of novel solidification-type bounds for random walks among non-elliptic random conductances, which should be of independent interest. 渗流理论大致可归类为对于以一定规则去掉给定图（如二维以上整数格点）中的顶点（或边）而产生的随机图的连通性的研究。近年来，对于具有长程代数衰减的相关性的渗流模型的研究正在不断深入。两个重要的基准模型是（离散的）高斯自由场的水平集（level set）和随机交织（random interlacements）的补集。在三维及以上的整数格点上，这两个模型都具有非平凡的渗流相变，该相变的特征是形成（几乎确定唯一的）无穷连通分支。前述两个基准模型中该相变的存在性和剧烈性（sharpness），以及模型在非临界区域的性质，已经被透彻地理解。一个特别令人感兴趣的问题是理解这些渗流模型中的界面和宏观的“空洞”是如何在“强超临界”情形下形成的。换言之，这些模型在何种情况下将会典型地产生占据大部分背景空间的无穷连通分支？本项目计划研究这些模型在具有（可能退化的）随机权重（可解释为杂质）的整数格点上的表现。在之前的工作中，我们在一致椭圆随机权重情形下已经获得了对形如“高斯自由场的下水平集将宏观集与给定外框的边界隔离开”的隔断（disconnection）事件的定量控制。我们的项目包含两个主要问题。首先，我们计划在具有一致椭圆随机权重的三维及以上整数格点上得到渗流相变的更精确的理解。其次，我们希望在三维及以上的非椭圆情形下（例如超临界伯努利渗流无穷簇上的高斯自由场的水平集或者随机交织模型的补集）建立对隔断事件的概率的控制，并同时研究二维情形下的相关问题。 本项目预计产生的成果将会进一步加深对杂质在长程渗流模型中的作用的理解，也将进一步发展非椭圆随机电导模型中的随机游走对应的凝固化（solidification）估计。该估计也具有独立的价值。

26302024.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26302024.value: 含双芳基环肽的高度应变全合成

26302024.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26302024.value: 纵观历史，包括抗生素和抗癌药物在内的制药产品在促进人类福祉方面发挥了至关重要的作用。然而，由于制药行业竞争激烈，发现针对特定蛋白质的新型小分子药物和抗体治疗变得越来越具有挑战性。这促使全球开始探索创新药物形式。相反，中分子治疗在近年来成为一个引人注目的重点领域。这些治疗方法相比小分子药物，具有更大且更复杂的结构，使它们能够展现更高的靶标特异性。因此，中分子治疗的发展在实现更高生理活性方面展现了巨大的潜力，并为疾病治疗和预防提供了有前景的路径。 在多种中分子治疗类别中，含有联芳基的手性环肽吸引了相当多的关注。这些肽具有一个在主链中结合联芳基团的环状结构，由于存在手性联芳单元而具有手性。这些手性联芳基团在芳基-芳基键周围具有受限旋转，赋予了环肽构象刚性并赋予其独特的结构和功能特性。在手性环肽中整合联芳基团提供了几个优势。首先，通过引入刚性元素，它增强了肽的结构稳定性，使其不易发生构象变化且更能抵抗蛋白水解降解。这种增强的稳定性在药物开发和药物化学应用中尤为有利。此外，手性环肽中联芳基团的加入，由于其独特的空间排列和电子特性，导致了多样的生物活性。这些肽可以对特定靶点（如蛋白质受体或酶）展现出强大的结合亲和力和选择性，因此在治疗和生物活性化合物开发中成为宝贵的工具。 本研究致力于探索高应变联芳基环肽。我们的主要目标是制定一种全面的方法，以构建手性选择性的Trp-Trp、Trp-His和Trp-Tyr键。此外，我们计划将这一新开发的方法应用于schischkiniin、roseovertin、strecintide 839、micitide 982、lapparbin和rubrin的全合成，这些化合物在合成尝试中迄今尚未成功。通过实现这些目标，我们的研究工作有望揭示合成高应变联芳基环肽的新途径，为选择性获取具有多种生物活性中分子提供宝贵的途径。

26302724.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26302724.value: 克服玻尔兹曼输运方程降阶模型中的Kolmogorov障碍

26302724.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26302724.value: The Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) is a high dimensional kinetic equation modeling particles interacting with a background medium. With its wide range of applications including medical imaging, remote sensing, astrophysics and nuclear fusion, efficient numerical simulations of BTE are greatly demanded but challenging due to its high dimensionality. As an attractive dimensionality reduction technique, data-driven reduced order models (ROMs) for BTE are highly desired and have rapidly advanced recently. These recently developed ROMs are linear ROMs that suffer from the Kolmogorov barrier in transport dominant problems. The Kolmogorov barrier means that the best error of approximating the underlying solution manifold with a linear space decays slowly as the space dimension grows. Limited by the optimal error, linear ROMs require high dimensional spaces, which reduce their efficiency, to maintain accuracy. When scattering and absorption effects are weak, transport dominant phenomena exist in BTE problems, leading to an efficiency decline of linear ROMs. Adaptive and nonlinear ROMs, exploiting piecewise linear or advanced nonlinear approximations, are designed to break the Kolmogorov barrier in other transport dominant problems. However, these techniques have not been thoroughly introduced or investigated for BTE. To bridge this gap, we aim to design time-adaptive and nonlinear ROMs to conquer the Kolmogorov barrier in time-dependent BTE problems with transport dominant phenomena. The proposed project comprises two parts. First, we will design a time-adaptive ROM for time-dependent BTE based on a novel adaptive time partitioning strategy. Employing a piecewise linear approximation in time, the proposed ROM can more effectively capture low-rank structures in time. To enhance its efficiency and accuracy, we will integrate it with spatial domain decomposition and parameter domain adaptation techniques. Additionally, we aim to establish a rigorous foundation for the effectiveness of mitigating the Kolmogorov barrier with piecewise linear in time approximations. Second, we will design nonlinear ROMs for BTE and incorporate them with the proposed time-adaptive ROM. Though more expensive to construct, nonlinear ROMs, exploiting advanced nonlinear approximations, are capable of efficiently capturing low rank structures that cannot be efficiently handled by linear or piecewise linear approximations. To balance construction efficiency and capability, we will design a hybrid ROM, which combines nonlinear ROMs with the proposed time-adaptive ROM, using nonlinear ROMs only when necessary. The output from this project will not only boost efficiency and accuracy of data-driven ROMs for BTE problems with transport dominant phenomena, but also contribute to the development of the ROM methodology. 玻尔兹曼输运方程（BTE）是一种高维动理学方程，它描述了粒子与背景介质之间的相互作用。由于其在医学成像、遥感、天体物理和核工程等领域的广泛应用，对BTE的高效数值模拟需求巨大，但也因这一方城的高维特性而具有挑战性。作为一种有效的降维技术，数据驱动的降阶模型（ROMs）吸引了广泛关注，并于最近快速进展。这些新开发的ROMs大多是是线性的降阶模型，而线性模型在传输主导的问题中会受到Kolmogorov障碍的不良影响。Kolmogorov障碍是指用线性空间逼近解流形的理论最优误差随着空间维度增加而缓慢下降的现象。受限于最优误差，线性ROMs中往往需要采用高维空间来保持准确性，从而降低了它们的效率。当散射和吸收效应较弱时，BTE问题中存在传输主导的现象，这会导致线性ROMs的效率下降。自适应和非线性ROMs利用分段线性或高级非线性逼近技术，来打破其他传输主导问题中的Kolmogorov障碍。然而，这些技术尚未在BTE中被彻底引入、研究。为了弥补这一空白，我们将设计时间自适应和非线性ROMs来克服传输主导的时变BTE问题中的Kolmogorov障碍。本研究项目包括两个部分。首先，我们将设计一种基于新型自适应时间分区策略的时变BTE的时间自适应ROM。采用时间上的分段线性逼近，所提出的ROM可以更有效地捕捉时间上的低秩结构。为了提高其效率和准确性，我们计划将其与空间域分解和参数域自适应技术相结合。此外，我们也希望建立一个时间分段线性逼近来缓解Kolmogorov障碍有效性的理论基础。第二，我们将为BTE设计非线性ROMs，并将其与提出的时间自适应策略结合起来。尽管构建成本较高，利用高级非线性逼近技术的非线性ROMs能高效地捕捉线性或分段线性逼近无法有效处理的低秩结构。为了平衡构建ROM付出的代价和ROM的逼近能力，我们希望设计一种混合的ROM，将非线性ROMs与第一部分中提出的时间自适应ROM相结合。这样，我们可以只在必要时才使用非线性ROMs。本项目的研究成果不仅将提升传输主导的BTE问题中数据驱动ROMs的效率和准确性，还将为ROM方法论的发展做出贡献。

26308524.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26308524.value: 拓扑反铁磁材料非线性输运的实验研究

26308524.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26308524.value: Topological antiferromagnets have emerged as a fertile platform for exploring various novel quantum transport phenomena, resulting from the intricate interplay between band topology, magnetism, and spin-orbit interactions. Research in this field is driven by the rich physics of these materials and their potential applications in energy-efficient spintronics, energy harvesting, and terahertz communication. Significant research has been dedicated to devising efficient methods for detecting and manipulating the Néel vector. Recently, nonlinear transport response has been theoretically proposed as a promising approach to probe and characterize antiferromagnetic order, marking significant progress in this area. However, there is a limited number of experimentally explored material candidates in this area. Specifically, topological antiferromagnets that exhibit nonlinear transport responses arising from both the Berry curvature dipole and quantum metric dipole mechanisms remain to be explored. Furthermore, effective strategies to engineer and control the nonlinear transport responses in these materials have not been systematically investigated. In this project, our primary focus is to utilize the nonlinear transport response as a highly sensitive tool for probing the Néel vector in topological antiferromagnets. Our initial research will revolve around studying topological antiferromagnetic materials that exhibit inversion symmetry breaking, even in the absence of magnetic ordering. In these proposed material systems, two crucial mechanisms, namely the Berry curvature dipole and quantum metric dipole, are simultaneously active, presenting a unique opportunity to assess their respective contributions to the nonlinear transport responses within a single material system. This investigation will contribute to the development of novel topological antiferromagnets with enhanced nonlinear transport responses. Furthermore, our research will explore the potential of electrical switching of the Néel vector and nonlinear transport detection of the Néel vector switch in topological antiferromagnets. We have identified three families of materials for this purpose. The electrical switching mechanism relies on the energy-efficient spin-orbit torque mechanism. By studying these effects, we aim to gain insights into the underlying physics and develop prototype devices for efficient control and detection of the Néel vector in antiferromagnetic systems. Additionally, we plan to investigate the nonlinear transport response as a means to explore strain-induced symmetry breaking in topological antiferromagnets. In this case, the origin of the symmetry breaking will extend beyond magnetic order to include charge order as well. The study of strain engineering of nonlinear transport responses holds great potential for the development of strain-engineered antiferromagnetic devices with tailored and customizable transport properties. 拓扑反铁磁材料已成为探索新型量子输运现象的重要平台，这些现象源于能带拓扑、磁性和自旋轨道相互作用的复杂相互作用。该领域的研究受到这些材料丰富的物理特性及其在低功耗自旋电子学、能量收集和太赫兹通信中潜在应用的驱动。目前，研究人员致力于开发检测和操纵反铁磁序的有效方法。最近，理论研究人员提出非线性输运响应可以作为一种有前景的方法来探测和表征反铁磁序，标志着该领域的一大重大进展。然而，当前实验上可以支持该研究的候选材料数量相当有限。特别是，具有由贝里曲率偶极子和量子度规偶极子机制共同引起的非线性输运响应的拓扑反铁磁材料仍有待探索。此外，对于这类材料的非线性输运响应的有效控制未得到系统地研究。 在本项目中，我们主要研究利用非线性输运响应作为探测拓扑反铁磁材料中反铁磁序的高灵敏手段。我们的初步研究将围绕一类在没有磁序的情况下也表现出非中心对称性的拓扑反铁磁材料展开。在这类材料系统，两个关键机制——贝里曲率偶极子和量子度规偶极子同时起作用。这为在单一材料系统中评估它们各自对非线性输运响应的贡献提供了独特的机会。这项研究将有助于开发具有增强非线性输运响应的新型拓扑反铁磁材料。此外，我们的研究还将探索利用电学方法改变反铁磁序的潜力，以及拓扑反铁磁材料中反铁磁序的非线性输运探测。为此，我们已经确定了三类材料，其电学改变反铁磁序的机制依赖于低功耗的自旋轨道扭矩。通过研究这些效应，我们旨在深入了解其背后的物理机制，并开发用于在反铁磁系统中有效控制和检测反铁磁序的原型器件。此外，我们还计划将非线性输运响应作为探索拓扑反铁磁体中应变诱导对称性破缺的手段。在这种情况下，对称性破缺的起源将超出磁序的范畴，还包括电荷序。研究非线性输运响应的应变工程对于开发具有特定输运性能的反铁磁器件有巨大潜力。

26309524.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26309524.value: 在Moire系统中有霍尔效应的拓扑相

26309524.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26309524.value: 在由堆叠和扭转二维材料形成的moire系统中取得的新进展，使得研究相互作用，拓扑和对称性成为可能，因为这种体系中参数非常可调，以及可探索很大的相空间。受到最近在moire体系中观测到的零磁场（分数）量子霍尔效应的启发，这份提议计划研究由这种物态而衍生或邻近此物态的拓扑相，这些拓扑相在电、热或自旋等方面有霍尔效应。我们提议用有效场论、平均场论和数值来进行研究。该课题对实现量子计算和高温超导具有潜在的应用意义。

26311224.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26311224.value: 利用泵浦-探测和二维红外光谱技术研究在振动强耦合下的超快分子动力学和化学过程

26311224.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26311224.value: 振动强耦合（Vibrational Strong Coupling，VSC）是近年来备受关注的现象，因其在凝聚相中操控化学反应的潜力而引起了越来越多的关注。振动强耦合发生在分子振动和腔体电磁模式之间的能量交换速度快于它们各自的寿命时。通常通过将高浓度的分子插入光学微腔（如法布里-珀罗（FP）腔）来实现此现象，从而使得腔体光子与分子振动之间形成杂化态的准粒子，称为分子振动极化基元（Molecular Vibrational Polaritons，MVPs）。Ebbesen等人的开创性工作表明，无需光激发，振动强耦合可以减缓或加速化学反应速率，甚至改变化学选择性，从而引领了极化子化学的新兴领域。最近泵浦-探测和二维红外（2D IR）光谱学的研究表明，振动强耦合可以影响分子间和分子内振动能传递，改变分子假旋转过程的动力学，并实现不同极化基元之间的非线性相互作用。 尽管振动强耦合被证实是一个利用光学空腔来改变化学反应的可行方法，但在推动该领域发展方面仍存在一系列挑战。这些挑战包括需要广泛探索振动强耦合应用的实验参数，将系统扩展到除六羰基钨之外的其他分子，研究更简单的化学过程以更好地理解机制，并探索振动强耦合与光化学的结合。 为了应对这些挑战，该提案旨在通过超快泵浦-探测和二维红外光谱学研究来探究四个主要目标： 1. 使用振动强耦合控制溶液中分子间和分子内振动能传递； 2. 在振动强耦合下测量水动力学； 3. 使用振动强耦合修改超快化学交换过程； 这个跨学科项目的预期结果是对振动强耦合下的超快分子动力学和过程的全面理解。这种理解可用于设计用于化学反应的强光-物质相互作用，从而有可能彻底改变极化子化学领域。该项目结合了超快光谱学、分子极化子、化学分析和纳米光子学方面的专业知识，使其在物理化学和光谱学领域具有创新性和颠覆性。通过解决极化子化学领域的挑战，该项目有望对在凝聚相中理解和控制化学反应做出重大贡献。

26311724.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26311724.value: 导出代数几何及其在研究Higgs丛和Hecke对应中的应用

26311724.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26311724.value: The proposed research focuses on employing recent advancements in Derived Algebraic Geometry (DAG) to address two intricate mathematical problems: (i)Understanding Higgs Bundles Moduli and Categorifying P=W Phenomenon: We investigate the deeper structures of Higgs bundle moduli spaces and the P=W phenomena using DAG. The groundbreaking P=W conjecture for GLn has recently been resolved, revealing deep cohomological structures tied to Hitchin systems. Our objective is to upgrade the P=W phenomenon to a categorical level by exploring the structures of derived categories associated with Hitchin systems and families of compactified Jacobians. (ii) Studying Hecke Correspondences of Moduli Spaces: We will study Hecke correspondences for curves and surfaces, which involve modifications of vector bundles and sheaves on varieties by points. Applying DAG to the study of Hecke correspondences, we aim to uncover new insights and structures within the derived categories of moduli spaces associated with curves and surfaces. Our approach will be based on recent developments in the area of Derived Algebraic Geometry (DAG). DAG, introduced by Lurie and Toen–Vezzos in the early 21st century, extends classical algebraic geometry by incorporating concepts from homotopy theory and higher category theory. DAG equips us with powerful tools to tackle previously elusive mathematical problems and reveal hidden structures within geometric objects. The proposed research also contributes to the “categorification” paradigm, which upgrades our understanding from the level of numbers to vector spaces and categories. In summary, our research employs the powerful tools of DAG to unlock the mysteries of Higgs bundle moduli spaces, Hitchin systems, and Hecke correspondences. It aims to provide new mathematical insights, potentially categorify the P=W phenomenon, and deepen our understanding of Hecke correspondences. While primarily advancing mathematical knowledge, these endeavours may also find practical applications in related fields. 该研究计划致力于用导出代数几何（DAG）的最新进展来解决两个复杂的数学问题： (i) 理解Higgs丛模空间和范畴化P=W现象。我们将使用DAG研究Higgs丛模空间和P=W现象的深层结构。GLn的P=W猜想最近已得到解决，揭示了与Hitchin系统相关的深层上同调结构。我们的目标是通过探索与Hitchin系统和紧化Jocobian簇相关的导出范畴的结构，将P=W现象提升到范畴层面。 (ii) 研究模空间的Hecke对应。我们将研究曲线和曲面的Hecke对应，这涉及到在点处对簇上的向量丛和层的修饰。应用DAG研究Hecke对应，旨在揭示与曲线和曲面相关的模空间的导出范畴内的新见解和结构。 我们的方法基于导出代数几何（DAG）领域的最新发展。DAG由Lurie和Toen-Vezzos在21世纪初引入，通过结合同伦理论和高阶范畴理论的概念，扩展了经典代数几何。DAG为我们提供了强大的工具来解决以前难以处理的数学问题，揭示几何对象的隐藏结构。此外，该研究还将推动“范畴化”范式，即从数值层面提升到向量空间和范畴层面的理解。 总的来说，我们的研究将利用DAG的强大工具来揭开Higgs丛模空间、Hitchin系统和Hecke对应的神秘面纱，提供新的数学见解，探索将P=W现象范畴化，并加深我们对Hecke对应的理解。尽管主要推动数学知识的发展，这些努力也可能在相关领域找到应用。

26501824.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26501824.value: 通过慈善活动应对负外部性：来自石油和天然气公司选择性的社区参与的证据

26501824.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501824.value: 本研究旨在探讨企业如何利用慈善活动来应对其经营活动的负外部性所引发的社区顾虑。我们提出，企业会在经营活动负外部性较高且存在相关顾虑的社区中增加慈善投入。这样一来，企业试图通过展示对社区的承诺来缓解这些顾虑。我们的识别策略将基于重大石油发现和披露法规的变化，以此来建立企业经营、负外部性与受影响社区慈善活动之间的因果关系。本研究还进一步考察了社区特征的地理差异对慈善行为的影响。尤其是我们通过分析社区对石油和天然气行业的经济依赖、意识形态取向和社会行动主义的影响来研究社区的异质性。其中，对行业经济依赖较大的社区可能对企业的威胁较小，因此获得的慈善捐助较少；而保守主义的社区可能会淡化环境问题，从而更少地产生由企业经营引发的顾虑。相反，社会行动主义水平较高的社区可能会使得企业产生声誉和监管的顾虑，从而获得更多的慈善支持。总体而言，本研究旨在增强我们对战略性企业慈善活动的理解，并阐明企业如何战略性地管理与负外部性相关的社区顾虑。

26504424.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26504424.value: 基础设施质量信息对政府支出和资源分配的影响

26504424.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504424.value: 这篇论文研究了基础设施质量信息是否会影响政府支出。政府经常进行调查以收集有关基础设施质量的数据。利用政府调查的分层随机抽样方法，本文比较了被抽样的基础设施与未被抽样的基础设施在资本支出和维护费用方面的差异。此外，本文还考察了政府是否会根据质量信息做出反应，向状况较差的被抽样基础设施分配更多资源，而不是状况良好的基础设施。基于包括资金来源（例如联邦拨款、州拨款或地方收入）、基础设施质量的替代衡量标准以及政府内部控制弱点的代理指标等横截面特征，进行了额外的分析。此研究为信息在资源分配中的作用文献作出了贡献。

26506124.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26506124.value: 人口老龄化与资产贬值风险--基于韩国养老基金的实证研究

26506124.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26506124.value: 这个项目旨在探究人口老龄化对整体股市估值和横截面股票价格的影响。具体来说，这个项目将研究不断加快的人口老龄化进程和具有刚性资产配置要求的大型公共养老金制度之间的相互作用所带来的潜在风险。这个实证研究有三个目标：（1）验证大型养老金基金净资本流入与股市估值之间是否存在因果关系；（2）如果存在这样的关系，定量估计养老金流入与估值之间的敏感性；（3）建立一个经济模型，利用这些估计来探索潜在的养老金改革方案。 该项目将重点关注韩国的国家养老金服务（NPS）。韩国作为全球生育率最低（每名妇女0.8个）的国家，而国家养老金基金持有超过7%的国内股市总值，是研究该问题的理想实验室。过去，由于人口增长，NPS的资产管理规模也成比例地增长。由于NPS的资产配置要求，资本流入股票市场，拉高了市场的整体估值。这种机制对未来的韩国股市构成了潜在威胁：不断缩小的NPS资产管理规模可能会对资产价格产生意外的下行压力。这意味着政策制定者可能依赖过于乐观的过去表现来进行耗尽情景和压力测试。 两个全球趋势使这个项目具有重要的现实意义。其一是世界各地广泛的人口老龄化，其二是公共养老金基金在金融市场中变得日益重要。大多数其他经济合作与发展组织（OECD）国家的生育率也在1.2至1.8之间。同时，OECD国家的养老金基金现在总资产管理规模超过38万亿美元。此外，这些资产管理规模对人口构成十分敏感。 尽管存在这样的全球趋势，但学界目前缺乏将人口老龄化和资产估值具体通过养老金基金联系起来的研究。现有的论文侧重于老龄化的宏观经济学（Lee, 2016；Mian et al., 2021；Acemoglu and Restrepo, 2022）。或者是研究老龄化对资产价格的影响（Poterba, 2001；Takats, 2010），但没有着眼于养老金基金。这是因为养老金基金在金融市场中的重要性是最近才被认识到的（Da et al., 2018；Greenwood and Vissing-Jorgensen, 2018；Aldunate etal.,2023）。此外，资产定价领域的研究越来越强调市场对资本流入的敏感性（Shleifer, 1986；van der Beck, 2022；Gabaix and Koijen, 2022）。这些现有研究进一步突显了研究老龄化引起的资本外流的意义所在。

26506524.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26506524.value: 信息披露频率、投资者视野和公司短视

26506524.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26506524.value: This proposed study aims to investigate the relationship between reporting frequency and corporate myopia by considering the impact of disclosure frequency in attracting investors with different investment horizons. The study will analyze the setting where interim reports can convey both interim performance information and signals that can be used to make inference on the long-term firm performance. This setting gives rise to the effect where changing the disclosure frequency can attract investors with different horizons. Investors with a long-term horizon can analyze the implications of current period earnings on the terminal cash flow of the company, while short-term investors benefit from the interim disclosures because these provide profit opportunities in the short run. However, more frequent disclosure may also affect the information advantage of short-run investors relative to uninformed investors. The study will also speak to financial market regulation on reporting frequency. Different countries have different quarterly reporting requirements, and many have discussed or are considering the potential effects of changing the financial reporting frequency. The study can potentially inform regulators about how the effect of reporting frequency on myopia may change depending on the information content of interim disclosures. Additionally, the study can provide insights into the optimal frequency of disclosure, considering different financial market environment and information environments. Furthermore, the study can provide insights into a firm's voluntary disclosure frequency choice. The research question can potentially speak to the trade-offs associated with voluntarily committing to more frequent information releases, such as retail companies providing voluntary monthly demand information or firms voluntarily providing quarterly report under the semi-annual reporting regime. Lastly, the study can provide insights into how certain disclosure attributes can help firms to attract investors with different investment horizons. While previous study has shown how better disclosure quality attracts different types of institutional investors, no other studies have examined how specific characteristics of firm disclosure attract investors with different characteristics. The study can potentially provide insights into whether more frequent disclosures can attract short- and long-term investors.

26508924.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26508924.value: 基于近似动态规划算法的排队网络最优控制

26508924.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26508924.value: Service systems often feature multiple classes of customers with different service needs and multiple pools of servers with different skillsets. How to efficiently match customers of different classes with servers of different skillsets, while balancing the tradeoff between system congestion and service quality, is of great importance to service system operations management. However, finding a good scheduling policy is challenging, especially for large-scale systems, due to the complicated system dynamics and intrinsic stochasticity. In this project, we aim to develop an approximate dynamic programming based method to solve a general queuing network control problem and provide theoretical performance guarantee. We will also study some complications brought by modern service operations management and apply the general framework to a healthcare application, the hospital patient flow management problem, where more practical issues are considered. The eventual goal is to deliver an applicable solution strategy that hospital managers can take as a reference to improve the hospital operations efficiency. 服务系统通常包含多个具有不同服务需求的客户类别和多个具有不同技能的服务团队。如何高效地将不同类别的客户与不同技能的服务人员进行匹配，同时平衡系统拥塞和服务质量之间的权衡，对于服务系统运营管理至关重要。然而，由于系统动态的复杂性和内在的随机性，找到一个好的调度策略尤其是在大规模系统中是非常具有挑战性的。在本项目中，我们旨在开发一种基于近似动态规划的方法，来解决一个通用的排队网络控制问题，并提供理论上的性能保证。我们还将研究现代服务运营管理带来的一些复杂问题，并将这一通用框架应用于一个医疗保健领域的实际案例——医院患者流动管理问题，在其中考虑到更多的实际问题。最终目标是提供一种适用的解决方案策略，以供医院管理者参考，从而提高医院运营效率。
